name: Cattail

facts.what: Spring shoots; early-summer pollen; rhizome starch
facts.how: Shoots raw or steamed; pollen as flour boost
facts.when: Shoots March to May, pollen May and June
facts.where: Ditches, tank edges, any standing fresh water

caution: Cattails filter their water, pollutants included, so harvest only from clean water you would trust. Before flower spikes appear, blue-flag iris shoots can fool a beginner: iris is flat-fanned and toxic, cattail is round-stemmed.

sections.title: Harvesting
sections.body: Grip a young shoot low and pull; the white base slides free like a leek. For pollen, bend a flowering head into a bag and tap: a minute of drumming yields golden tablespoons.

sections.title: In the kitchen
sections.body: The shoot hearts taste of cucumber and leek, good raw or barely steamed. Pollen folds into pancake batter for color and a corn-silk sweetness.
